testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you watch out for black ice?

options.text: When it is snowing.
When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when it is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?

options.text: No, it is not recommended.
Yes, it is required.
No, it is optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Drive straight forward, then straight back.
Drive straight back, then forward to the left.
Drive straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, drive straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What does it mean when you see taillights ahead while driving in fog?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can be sure the vehicle is on the road.
It may be a trick of the eye.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not reliable for finding the road. A vehicle's lights may come from a vehicle that has left the road.

questions.question: What should you do when stopped on the side of the road?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.
Turn on the emergency flashers.
Wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What must you do if convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car?

options.text: Tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction, regardless of what vehicle you were driving. This does not include parking violations.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have a low center of gravity.
They usually have a high center of gravity.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks usually have high centers of gravity. You must be careful when driving them because their contents can shift during transport.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT mean your brakes are bad?

options.text: Cracked drums
Pads with no oil or grease on them
Very thin shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn too thin. Clean pads without oil or grease are fine.

questions.question: How should you adjust your mirrors before driving?

options.text: No part of your vehicle should appear in any mirror.
Part of your vehicle should appear in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should appear in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your vehicle helps you judge where other objects are located.

questions.question: How does fatigue affect a driver?

options.text: It usually makes them more alert.
It usually makes them more careful.
It makes them slower to make important decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes them slower to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers react slower to hazards than rested drivers. Drowsy drivers cannot make critical decisions as quickly.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Provide extra storage.
Protect the driver from cargo that shifts forward.
Have no benefits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts forward.
questions.explanation: Header boards protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start going down the hill.
After you have started going down the hill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster going down a hill.

questions.question: What do you need to transport a load that is too long?

options.text: Special permits.
A convoy to stop all traffic.
A person to walk next to the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Special permits.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy may need special permits. Some loads may also need a pilot vehicle with warning signs or a police escort.

questions.question: After you change a tire, what should you do after driving a short distance?

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check if rocks are stuck in the tire tread.
Polish the tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: Where should regrooved tires not be used?

options.text: On any vehicle.
On the front wheels of a bus.
On trucks carrying gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.

options.text: Three points of contact
Four points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact as you exit. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: As a truck driver, what is NOT your responsibility?

options.text: Inspecting the cargo.
Checking if the weight is balanced properly.
Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your cargo, check for overloading or poor weight balance, ensure the cargo is secure and does not block your view, and ensure it does not cover emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: What is true about dual tires?

options.text: Both tires should not touch the road.
The tires should not touch each other.
The tires should be different sizes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires should not touch each other.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open the load to check safety.
Make sure the weight does not exceed the limit.
Look inside the container before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the weight does not exceed the limit.
questions.explanation: You cannot open a sealed load to inspect it. However, you must still make sure the weight does not exceed the allowed limit.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded onto a truck?

options.text: The person who loaded the truck.
The company supervisor.
The truck driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver.
questions.explanation: The truck driver is responsible for the cargo. Even if someone else loaded it, the driver must inspect it and make sure it is secure.

questions.question: If you have more than one license, what happens?

options.text: You likely won't be caught.
You should not tell anyone.
You can be caught through a shared computer system between states.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be caught through a shared computer system between states.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent one person from getting multiple licenses. It is illegal to have more than one driver's license.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle, what should you NOT check?

options.text: Too much air pressure in your tires.
Too little air pressure in your tires.
The brand name of your tires matches.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brand name of your tires matches.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that your tire air pressure is not too high or too low. You do not need to check if all tires are the same brand.

questions.question: Which tire condition should NOT concern you?

options.text: Too much air pressure
At least 4/32 inch of tread on front tires
Mixing radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 4/32 inch of tread on front tires
questions.explanation: Front tires should have at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires should have at least 2/32 inch. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires together or use tires of different sizes.

questions.question: What happens when you accelerate roughly?

options.text: It can damage the vehicle.
It is normal for a warmed-up vehicle.
It improves fuel economy.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up slowly and smoothly so the vehicle doesn't jerk. Rough acceleration can cause damage to the engine and transmission.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.
Push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction inside the brake drum is created when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Drivers behind a truck:

options.text: May not see objects in front of the truck.
Usually have a clear view of the road ahead.
Do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not see objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They may not see hazards ahead. Flash your brake lights and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A second conviction of operating a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher results in:

options.text: Loss of your CDL for one year.
Loss of your CDL for five years.
Loss of your CDL for life.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: A first conviction of operating a commercial vehicle with BAC of 0.04 percent or higher results in losing your CDL for one year. A second conviction results in losing your CDL for life.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer.
The weight rating of a tire.
The weight rating per axle of a combination vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight that the manufacturer says a single vehicle can safely carry.

questions.question: You should slow down and be extra careful when:

options.text: Traveling in normal traffic.
Driving on dry pavement.
Approaching a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approaching a work zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where the road edge drops off, when there are objects on the road, and on freeway ramps.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Prohibited.
Acceptable in clear weather.
Allowed if it is work-related.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire:

options.text: Open the hood.
Turn off the engine.
Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as safely possible. Do not open the hood while putting out the fire.

questions.question: On long drives, you should:

options.text: Take rest breaks.
Drive as fast as possible.
Drive through the night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours to avoid fatigue. Driving when you are normally asleep is dangerous.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should never be done.
Should be done to stop cargo from shifting.
Should only be done with welded material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done to stop cargo from shifting.
questions.explanation: Block cargo to prevent it from sliding around. Shifting cargo makes steering and handling harder.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Leave the roadway as soon as safely possible
Keep driving normally

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: Safely leave the roadway and park your vehicle right away. Low air pressure means your brakes may not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Drivers cannot operate a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.1 percent.
0.04 percent.
0.08 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.04 percent.
questions.explanation: You will lose your CDL for at least one year if your BAC is 0.04 percent or higher. Driving a CMV while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Causing a death by careless operation of a CMV will result in losing your CDL for at least:

options.text: One month.
Six months.
One year.

questions.correctAnswerText: One year.
questions.explanation: A first conviction for causing a death by careless operation of a CMV means losing your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: To make your vehicle more visible during the day, you should:

options.text: Use your low beam headlights.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your clearance lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights for best visibility during the day. High beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: Cargo should be covered:

options.text: To protect people from spillage.
To hide the materials.
To make it harder to steal.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect people from spillage.
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm others
Operating an unsafe motor vehicle
Operating a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm others
questions.explanation: Road rage is driving with the intent to harm others or physically assault another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:

options.text: Thin.
Properly tight.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tight.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you use the brake pedal?

options.text: Push down gradually.
Push down quickly.
Pull up gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Why are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly
To provide extra gears
To improve gas mileage

questions.correctAnswerText: To provide extra gears
questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
When you have a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces the need for braking. However, it can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn off retarders when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: How should mirrors be properly adjusted?

options.text: No part of the vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
A small part of the vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small part of the vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted mirror shows some of your vehicle. This helps you judge how far away other objects are from your vehicle.

questions.question: What vehicle must you use for the on-road driving skills test?

options.text: You can use any type of vehicle for the test.
You must use the same type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
The vehicle type does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the same type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take the on-road skills test with the same type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in a vehicle?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials
Only during interstate travel
Yes, it is required

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required
questions.explanation: Emergency equipment is required. Check for it during a pre-trip inspection. Required items include spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through flowing water or a large puddle?

options.text: Speed up
Slow down and gently apply the brakes
Stop in the water

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gently apply the brakes
questions.explanation: Try to avoid driving through water. If you must drive through it, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of the brake system.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old
Because water and oil collect in the tanks
To change the pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because water and oil collect in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks regularly, at least at the end of each day, to remove these materials.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Stay fit and healthy
Keep the cab warm
Eat heavy foods

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay fit and healthy
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and warm cabs make you drowsy. Exercise and eat healthy to stay alert while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a construction worker near the road?

options.text: Speed up
Slow down
Move to the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully through work zones. Reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.
